title: Parables IQ
subtitle: Can you tell a real parable from a fake one?

questions.text: In the parable of the Good Samaritan, who walked past the wounded man before the Samaritan helped him?

options.explanation: Luke 10:31-32 — a priest passed by on the other side, then a Levite did the same, before the Samaritan stopped.
Pharisees and scribes were the audience Jesus often addressed, but they are not the ones in this parable.

options.text: A tax collector and a soldier
options.explanation: Neither appears in this parable; the two who passed by were religious officials.
That's closer to the Unforgiving Servant parable in Matthew 18.

questions.text: What did the father give the prodigal son when he returned home?

options.text: A scroll of forgiveness and a horse
options.explanation: The text gives no scroll and no horse; it speaks of a robe, ring, shoes, and a feast.

options.text: The best robe, a ring, and shoes — and a feast with the fatted calf
options.explanation: Luke 15:22-23 — the father called for the best robe, a ring on his finger, shoes on his feet, and the fatted calf for the feast.
That phrase belongs to King Ahasuerus in Esther, not the prodigal's father.
The father didn't stay silent — he rejoiced loudly and ordered a celebration.

questions.text: Which of these is NOT one of the soils in the Parable of the Sower?

options.explanation: Matthew 13:4 — "some seeds fell by the way side" is one of the four soils.
Matthew 13:5 — stony ground is the second soil.
There is no "sandy shore" soil. The four soils are wayside, stony, thorny, and good ground.
Matthew 13:7 — thorny ground is the third soil.

questions.text: In the parable of the talents, how many talents did the master give the wicked servant?

options.explanation: The servant given five talents doubled them to ten and was praised.
The servant given two talents also doubled them and was praised.
Matthew 25:18 — "he that had received one went and digged in the earth, and hid his lord's money."
Ten talents is what the first servant ended up with after doubling his five.

questions.text: Which of these is NOT a real parable of Jesus?

options.explanation: Matthew 13:45-46 — Jesus did tell this parable.

options.text: The Two Builders on Rock and Sand
options.explanation: Matthew 7:24-27 — this concludes the Sermon on the Mount.

options.text: The Three Lamps on the Hillside
options.explanation: Jesus told a parable about one lamp not being put under a basket (Matthew 5:15), but there is no "three lamps on a hillside" parable.
Matthew 13:24-30 — Jesus told this parable about the enemy who sowed tares among wheat.

questions.text: In the parable of the Good Shepherd, what does the shepherd do for the sheep?

options.explanation: The emphasis isn't on counting.

options.text: Lays down his life for them
options.explanation: John 10:11 — "I am the good shepherd: the good shepherd giveth his life for the sheep."

options.text: Sells the weak ones for profit
options.explanation: That's the opposite of the Good Shepherd; the hireling abandons the sheep.
Jesus leaves the ninety-nine to seek the one lost sheep (Luke 15:4).

questions.text: In the parable of the Ten Virgins, what did the foolish virgins forget to bring?

options.explanation: The wedding garment shows up in a different parable (Matthew 22:11).
Matthew 25:3 — "They that were foolish took their lamps, and took no oil with them."
The parable doesn't mention a gift for the bridegroom.
All ten were invited; the issue was the oil.

questions.text: Which lesson best matches the parable of the Mustard Seed?

options.text: Hidden things will eventually be exposed
options.explanation: That's a different teaching (Mark 4:22).

options.text: The kingdom starts small but grows greater than any herb
options.explanation: Matthew 13:31-32 — the mustard seed is least of seeds, but becomes a tree where the birds lodge in its branches.

options.text: You must wait patiently for harvest
options.explanation: Closer to the Seed Growing Secretly (Mark 4:26-29).
That phrase is from James 2:26, not from Jesus' parables.

questions.text: In the parable of the Unforgiving Servant, how much did the master forgive him?

options.explanation: A hundred pence is what the servant refused to forgive his fellow servant.
Matthew 18:24 — "one was brought unto him, which owed him ten thousand talents" — an astronomically large debt.
Thirty pieces of silver was the price paid to Judas, not from this parable.
Two mites was the widow's offering in Mark 12:42.

questions.text: Which line is from the parable of the Rich Fool, not an inspirational quote?

options.text: "God will never give you more than you can handle"
options.explanation: That phrase is not in the Bible at all — it's modern Christian folklore.

options.text: "Soul, thou hast much goods laid up for many years; take thine ease, eat, drink, and be merry"
options.explanation: Luke 12:19 — the rich man's self-talk just before God called him a fool that very night.
A modern Christian saying, not Scripture.
Not in the Bible — often attributed to a Persian fable.

questions.text: In the parable of the Lost Sheep, how many sheep did the shepherd leave to find the one?

options.explanation: Not the number Jesus gave.
Luke 15:4 — "What man of you, having an hundred sheep, if he lose one of them, doth not leave the ninety and nine?"
Not in this parable.
Not in this parable.

questions.text: Which of these is a real parable of Jesus?

options.text: The Two Coins and the Banker
options.explanation: There is no such parable. The closest is the Widow's Mite, but that's a real event, not a parable.
Jesus said if the disciples were silent the stones would cry out (Luke 19:40), but no parable carries this title.
Luke 18:9-14 — Jesus told this parable about the proud Pharisee and the humble tax collector who went home justified.
There's a centurion story (Matthew 8) and a vineyard parable (Matthew 21), but no combined "Centurion's Vineyard" parable.

scoring.perfectMessage: Twelve for twelve — the Teacher Himself would smile.
